在奈及利亞約魯巴音樂中，岡科圭雙鐘出現於伊佩塞鼓合奏、伊法祭典與安撫神靈儀式，也: In Yoruba music in Nigeria the gankogui appears in ìpèsè drum ensembles, in Ifá rites and in ceremonies to appease the deities, and it is used in sub-genres such as jùjú, Afro-jùjú, apala and fuji. In Brazil it is found in Candomblé ritual, in capoeira accompaniment and in 1920s choro ensembles, played alongside the seven-string guitar and the shaker; it has entered samba drum sections and carnival, and is used in popular songs to lay down a non-Brazilian groove; it can also supply special effects for ad hoc dance tunes or Latin suites.

岡科圭雙鐘是體鳴樂器，屬無舌鐘類，霍恩博斯特尔—薩克斯編號111.242。其構造: The gankogui is an idiophone of the clapperless bell type, Hornbostel-Sachs number 111.242. It is built from two pieces of iron, each bent into a tube, one large and one small, joined by a bent iron rod; to play it you hold the handle in one hand with the mouths facing out and the small bell on top, and strike the bells with a wooden or metal stick. Bells of this kind come from West Africa and are associated with the Yoruba, Edo and other peoples; they are also found in Nigerian religious and popular music and were carried to Brazil, where they are used in Candomblé, capoeira, choro and samba.

此類雙鐘由兩片金屬錐形管以U形金屬棒相連，屬無舌體鳴樂器。敲擊不同鐘體產生不同音: These double bells are two conical metal tubes joined by a U-shaped metal rod, and they are struck idiophones with no clapper. Striking the two bells gives two pitches: the longer bell sounds lower, the shorter higher; the thickness of the wall matters too, a thick wall vibrating less and a thin wall more readily. Compared with a single cowbell, the double-bell structure offers two pitches, and it is struck with a drumstick or a wooden or metal beater. The source does not mention any means of controlling volume.
演奏時以單手握持彎柄，使柄位於掌心，兩個鐘口朝外，較小鐘在上、較大鐘在下。發聲以: Hold the bent handle in one hand with the handle in your palm, the two mouths facing out, the smaller bell above and the larger below. Sound it by striking the bells with a drumstick or a wooden or metal beater. For a beginner the points are to keep that orientation and to tell the pitches apart by the length of the bells: the long bell is low, the short one high; the thickness of the wall affects the vibration as well, a thick wall vibrating less and a thin wall more readily.
發聲體為兩個金屬鐘，早期以鍛鐵製成，現以多種金屬與尺寸製作，以產生不同音色。鐘體: The sounding bodies are two metal bells, made of wrought iron at first and now of various metals and sizes to produce different timbres. The bell is a fan-shaped sheet of iron rolled into a cone, and the two bells are welded together with a horseshoe-shaped metal piece; another source records sheet iron bent into one large and one small tube, joined by a bent iron rod. The beater may be of wood or metal; the materials of the other parts are not stated.

阿哥哥鈴起源於西非，約魯巴、埃多、伊多馬與伊加拉等族群以單鐘或雙鐘形式使用。其名: The agogo bell comes from West Africa, where the Yoruba, Edo, Idọma and Igbira peoples use it as a single or a double bell. Its name and its making travelled to the Americas with enslaved West Africans, and in Brazil it entered Candomblé, capoeira, 1920s choro ensembles and samba drum sections, becoming part of secular carnival rhythm. In Nigeria it is used in the ìpèsè drumming of Ifá rites and appears in genres such as jùjú, Afro-jùjú, apala and fuji. Its material has widened from wrought iron to many metals and sizes, and the pitch changes with the length of the bell and the thickness of its wall.
